a longer duration (≥6 months) of lactation was related to higher fT3 concentrations 9–16 y postpartum among women with history GDM.
a longer duration (≥6 months) of lactation was associated with greater serum fT TSH and fT4 levels 9–16 year postpartum among women with a history GDM.
a longer duration lactation is associated with increased fT3 levels 9–16 y after delivery among Danish women with GDM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between lactation duration and postpartum thyroid function among women in the high-risk population of GDM.
the association between lactational history and thyroid function.
the relationship between lactation and thyroid function among women who have a history of gestational hyperglycemia and are at risk of developing future metabolic complications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
longer lactation duration is not related to thyroid function in women with GDM.
longer lactation duration may be related to higher fT3, but not fT4 levels in women with history of GDM, but this association may be driven by parity and needs further confirmation.
lactation is associated with a higher fT4 level, but not TSH and fT3, among women with history for GDM, and that the association was more evident in women with only one lifetime pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lactation is associated with increased thyroid function among women who had GDM during pregnancy.
lactation is a protective factor for long-term thyroid function, and this may be of particular relevance to women with GDM.
lactation is associated with increased fT3 and fT3:FT4 ratio, which may be a consequence of increased energy expenditure during lactation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lactation is a protective factor for the risk of cardiometabolic disease in women with GDM.
lactation may have a positive effect on long-term thyroid function in a population with high risk of cardiometabolic complications, but further studies are needed to confirm this association.
